The test image shows: multiple sugarcane plants/tillers with extensively browned/dried leaves, dark blackened base/stem area, and dying foliage with some remaining green at growing points. This suggests a systemic or basal disease. Top candidates: Grassy_Shoot, Sett_Rot, Leaf_Scald, Yellow_Leaf.

Now viewing one reference per candidate class:

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Multiple sugarcane plants/tillers clustered at base, leaves extensively browned/dried, dark blackened base area, dense proliferation of thin shoots, with some residual green at growing tips.

- **Grassy_Shoot (LeafNet_107)**: Strong match — same dense clustering of many thin shoots at the base, mix of brown/dried and green leaves, same ground-level perspective showing proliferating tillers. Grassy_Shoot causes abnormal proliferation of many small thin shoots.

- **Sett_Rot (LeafNet_136)**: Shows completely dead/dried plants with dark bases — shares dark base coloring but plants are more uniformly dead; test image still has active green growth.

- **Leaf_Scald (SugarLeaf_ID_131)**: Close-up of individual leaf with white streak lesion — completely different from test image.

- **Yellow_Leaf (LeafNet_182)**: Shows yellowing/browning of individual leaves with green mixed in — similar colors but wrong morphology (no multiple shoot proliferation).

The dominant feature in the test image is the dense proliferation of multiple thin shoots/tillers at the soil level, which is the hallmark symptom of Grassy_Shoot disease. The browning/drying is secondary progression of the disease.
